title: Real-time monitoring of CD8+ T and myeloid cell behavior in ovarian cancer slices
author: Laforêts, Donnadieu, et al.
materials: This major step consists of staining and mounting the ex vivo tumor slices for fluorescent live imaging. This includes blocking the Fc receptor, staining malignant cells, the extracellular matrix (fibronectin), CD8+ T cells and myeloid cells with antibodies directly conjugated to fluorochromes; and mounting the stained slices in an imaging dish containing unsupplemented phenol red-free RPMI 1640 media.6.Block Fc Receptors.a.After the minimum 10 min incubation time and a maximum of 24 h at 37°C, transfer the slice to a 30 mm petri dish using forceps and place the stainless-steel washer back on top of the tissue.b.Add 20 μL undiluted human TruStain inside the ring, on top of the tissue.c.Incubate 15 min at 37°C.d.Remove the blocking solution.7.Immunofluorescence staining.a.Prepare the antibody mix.i.Each antibody dilution must be empirically optimized. We recommend 50 μg/mL as a starting concentration. Table 1 shows the antibody mix we have used:Table 1Antibody panel for real-time imaging of myeloid and CD8+ T cells in human ovarian tumor slicesTargetMarkerDyeDilutionManufacturerCatalogue numberCytotoxic T cellsCD8Alex Fluor 6471:10BioLegend344725Myeloid cellsCD11bAlex Fluor 5941:10BioLegend301340Malignant cellsEpCAMAlex Fluor 4881:10Thermo Fisher Scientific53-8326-42Extracellular matrixFibronectinAlex Fluor 4051:10Novus biologicalsNBP2-34633AF405ii.Antibodies are diluted in unsupplemented phenol red-free RPMI 1640.iii.When optimizing, include a single staining with each antibody.iv.Also include a slice that will not be stained to assess tissue autofluorescence.b.Add 20 μL of antibody mix (or phenol red-free RPMI 1640 if assessing autofluorescence) inside the stainless-steel washer, on top of the tissue.c.Incubate slices with antibody mix for 15 min at 37°C.d.Remove antibody mix.e.Wash slices with phenol red-free RPMI 1640.i.Add 40 μL phenol red-free RPMI 1640 on top of the tissue, pipette up and down and discard the media.ii.Add another 40 μL of fresh phenol red-free RPMI 1640.iii.Incubate 2 min at 37°C.iv.Discard washing media and replace with 40 μL of fresh phenol red-free RPMI 1640.v.Incubate 2 min at 37°C.vi.Discard washing media.8.Mount the slices (Methods video S7).a.Using forceps, remove the stainless-steel washer, carefully flip and transfer the slice into a 30 mm glass bottom dish.CRITICAL: It is important to flip the slice, as the stained side must face down for imaging with an inverted microscope. If using an upright microscope, do not flip the slice.Optional: If necessary, before transferring the slice, add 100 μL of phenol red-free RPMI 1640 on top of the slice and another 100 μL around it to make it easier to pick up.Optional: It is possible to mount up to four slices together in the same dish (recommended if imaging multiple slices). For this, the agarose around the tissue must be gently trimmed using a scalpel, in order for all slices to fit on the glass bottom of the imaging dish. In addition, we recommend trimming the side of the agarose slice that faces other slices to ensure that all slices fit inside the tissue slice anchor. As the mounting of multiple slices on the same dish can take time, ensure that all slices stay hydrated by adding 20 μL phenol red-free RPMI 1640 to them after transferring them to the imaging dish.b.Add the tissue slice anchor on top of the tissue. Ensure it is positioned in such a way that it surrounds all tissue slices and does not lie on top.CRITICAL: First dip the anchor in phenol red-free RPMI 1640. When the anchor is dry, it is hydrophobic and is likely to float when filling the imaging dish with media, which in turn can move the slices.c.Slowly add 1 mL phenol red-free RPMI 1640 (imaging media) on top of the slice(s) with a P1000. Ensure neither the tissue slice(s) nor the anchor move in the process. Place the lid back on top of the imaging dish before transporting to the microscope.

steps.title: Set up peristaltic pump & oxygenate media
steps.instruction: Assemble a two‑channel peristaltic pump system and oxygenate the imaging media for live imaging of tumor slices.

substeps.instruction: Place the peristaltic pump (model 120S/DM2) outside the temperature‑controlled chamber on a surface separate from the microscope to avoid vibration.
Attach two sets of bioprene tubing to the pump, one set per channel.
Prepare the carbogen (95% O₂/5% CO₂) cylinder:
i. Set the regulator to 0.1 bar.
ii. Connect the gas outlet to a bioprene tube (tube end 1).
iii. Connect tube end 2 to a 2 mL plastic pipette; this pipette will later be inserted into a stopper with two holes in the oxygenated media flask.
Insert a 2 mL plastic pipette into the bioprene in‑flow tube (tube end 3) for later insertion in the stopper.
Prepare two bent 19G, 40 mm needles by bending 6–8 mm from the tip, wash them and keep in ethanol; they will later be attached to in‑flow tube end 4 and out‑flow tube end 5.
Set up a waste conical flask (≥1 L) outside the chamber:
i. Add 100 mL Virkon.
ii. Place a single‑hole stopper on the flask.
iii. Insert a 2 mL plastic pipette into the stopper.
iv. Insert the upper end of the pipette into the out‑flow section of the bioprene tubing (tube end 6).
Fill a 500 mL conical flask with at least 250 mL phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640 (imaging media).
Connect the carbogen cylinder (regulator set to 0.1 bar) to the bioprene tube (end 1) whose end 2 is plunged into the imaging media to gently bubble the medium.
Connect the pump tubing:
• In‑flow section: end 3 immersed in the bubbled imaging media; end 4 fitted with a bent needle immersed in the imaging dish.
• Out‑flow section: end 5 fitted with a bent needle immersed in the imaging dish; the other end (tube end 6) leads to the waste flask.
Place both the imaging dish and the oxygenated media flask inside the temperature‑controlled imaging chamber set to 37 °C and 5 % CO₂.

Use bioprene tubing with 1.6 mm bore and 1.6 mm wall inside the pump, connected via tube connectors to tubing with 0.8 mm bore and 1.6 mm wall that fits the 2 mL pipette and 19G needles (critical detail).

steps.title: Block Fc receptors on slice
steps.instruction: Incubate the tumor slice with human TruStain to block Fc receptors before antibody staining.

substeps.instruction: After a minimum of 10 min and a maximum of 24 h incubation at 37 °C, transfer the slice to a 30 mm petri dish using forceps and place the stainless‑steel washer back on top of the tissue.
Add 20 µL undiluted human TruStain inside the washer ring, directly on the tissue.
Incubate for 15 min at 37 °C.
Remove the blocking solution.

steps.title: Perform immunofluorescence staining
steps.instruction: Stain malignant cells, extracellular matrix, CD8⁺ T cells and myeloid cells with fluorophore‑conjugated antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the antibody mix in phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640:
• Use a starting concentration of 50 µg/mL for each antibody (empirically optimize).
• Antibody panel (catalog numbers included):
– CD8 (Cytotoxic T cells) – Alex Fluor 647, 1:10 dilution, BioLegend, Cat 344725
– CD11b (Myeloid cells) – Alex Fluor 594, 1:10 dilution, BioLegend, Cat 301340
– EpCAM (Malignant cells) – Alex Fluor 488, 1:10 dilution, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Cat 53‑8326‑42
– Fibronectin (Extracellular matrix) – Alex Fluor 405, 1:10 dilution, Novus Biologicals, Cat NBP2‑34633AF405
• Include single‑stain controls for each antibody and an unstained slice to assess tissue autofluorescence.
Add 20 µL of the antibody mix (or phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640 for autofluorescence control) inside the stainless‑steel washer on top of the tissue.
Incubate for 15 min at 37 °C.
Remove the antibody mix.
Wash the slice:
i. Add 40 µL phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640, pipette up and down, discard the media.
ii. Add another 40 µL fresh phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640, incubate 2 min at 37 °C, discard.
iii. Add 40 µL fresh phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640, incubate 2 min at 37 °C, discard.

steps.title: Mount slices in imaging dish
steps.instruction: Place stained slice(s) into a glass‑bottom dish, add anchor and imaging media, and prepare for microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Using forceps, carefully remove the stainless‑steel washer, flip the slice so the stained side faces down (required for inverted microscopes; do not flip for upright microscopes), and transfer it into a 30 mm glass‑bottom dish.
Optional handling aid: add 100 µL phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640 on top of the slice and another 100 µL around it before transfer.
If mounting up to four slices in the same dish:
• Trim the surrounding agarose with a scalpel so all slices fit on the glass bottom.
• Trim the side of the agarose that faces other slices to allow the tissue‑slice anchor to surround all slices.
• After transfer, add 20 µL phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640 to keep the slices hydrated.
Dip the tissue‑slice anchor in phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640 (dry anchor becomes hydrophobic and may float).
Place the anchor on top of the tissue, ensuring it surrounds all slices without lying on them.
Slowly add 1 mL phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640 (imaging media) on top of the slice(s) using a P1000 pipette, taking care that neither the slices nor the anchor move.
Replace the lid on the imaging dish and transport the dish to the microscope.

steps.title: Prepare data directory and run R analysis
steps.instruction: Organize Imaris output files and execute the provided R script to generate aggregated cell‑behavior statistics.

substeps.instruction: Create a single working folder.
Inside it, place all Imaris output folders (one folder per film). Each folder must contain CSV files named "_[statistic].csv".
If you have two films per slice, name the folders with the same base (e.g., slice1_a and slice1_b).
Open "Aggregate_stats.R" in RStudio.
Run lines 12‑13 to install and load the required package:
> install.packages("tidyverse")
> library(tidyverse)
Edit lines 16‑17 to set the working directory path (e.g., setwd("C:/Your/Path")) and assign the folder list variable.
Run lines 27‑89. The script will:
• Iterate over each film folder, load the statistic CSVs, calculate maximum displacement per track, and write a "__Max_Displacement.csv" file.
• Read length, speed and straightness files, merge them by track ID, and write an "Allstats.csv" for each film.
If a slice has only one film (non‑paired):
i. Create a separate folder anywhere.
ii. Move its "All stat.csv" into this folder.
iii. Rename it to "All stat.merged.csv".
Run lines 94‑107 to merge paired‑film "Allstats" files (the script loops over file pairs and writes merged files named "Allstats.merged.csv").
Place the renamed non‑paired merged files back into the main working directory.
Run the remaining script lines (117‑752) to complete the analysis.

Verify that the working directory now contains per‑cell statistic CSVs and per‑slice mean CSVs for trajectory length, mean speed and straightness, for categories: all, st, wob, mig, Lmig, mig2, and a proportion file.

steps.title: Organize outputs, plot data and perform statistics
steps.instruction: Finalize data handling, generate plots, and apply appropriate statistical tests.

substeps.instruction: Confirm that the working directory holds both individual‑cell and sample‑mean CSV files for each movement statistic (trajectory length, mean speed, straightness) and for each cell‑population category (all, st, wob, mig, Lmig, mig2) plus the proportion file.
Repeat the entire data‑preparation and R‑script execution (steps 1‑3 above) for CD11b (myeloid) cell movement data.
Plot the results:
a. Histogram (with individual data points) of a chosen statistic where each point represents the mean of all cells for a slice.
b. Plot of the same statistic for each individual cell.

Note: Method a. gives more weight to individual samples and ignores cell‑number differences; method b. gives more weight to individual cells and may increase statistical significance. Consider reporting absolute differences or percentages relative to control means.
Assess normality of each dataset before choosing a statistical test.
For two‑condition comparisons, use a parametric t‑test (both plotting methods).
For three or more conditions, use a parametric one‑way ANOVA.
